reasons: Three of the ten sections were not available, so the whole behaviour is not known.
The exports used by the home data file are not visible here.

terms.meaning: one half of the brain; here it names the left and right sides of the map
a labelled group of points on one side, such as Roles
a link that comes from the real data, as opposed to a family link, which only groups a cluster

used_by: The hero brain component (not visible in this packet)

sections.name: File setup, Hemisphere
sections.title: Imports and side type
sections.what: Explains the left and right split and brings in the battle, build, project, curiosity, research, skill, model and photo data.
sections.why: Gives the file one set of inputs and a clear split between work and curiosity.
sections.watch_out: The imported modules that are not visible here must still exist, or the file fails to load.

sections.name: BrainRegion
sections.title: Region shape
sections.what: Describes a labelled group on one side of the brain with a one-letter code.
sections.why: The letter labels point codes so visitors can see which group a point is from.

sections.name: BrainNode
sections.title: Point shape
sections.what: Describes a point on the brain: its code, group, side, label, optional line of text, optional image, optional link and optional industry sheet.
sections.why: One shape covers every point on the map.
sections.watch_out: Image paths must match the public folder layout; the route strips the leading slash before sending them.

sections.name: BrainLink
sections.title: Link shape
sections.what: Describes a connection between two points and whether it comes from the data or only groups a cluster.
sections.why: The kind lets the map draw facts differently from groupings.
sections.watch_out: Family links are kept here but filtered out before the home page receives them.

sections.name: brainRegions, regionOf, nodes, links, count
sections.title: Region list and counters
sections.what: Defines the fixed regions on each side, plus model family regions from the mental model list, each with a letter, and sets up empty lists for points, links and counters.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed region list keeps the map layout stable.
sections.watch_out: Model family letters come from fixed lists of five on the left and three on the right, so extra families get no letter.

sections.name: add
sections.title: Add a point to a region
sections.what: Adds one point to a region, giving it the next number in that region as its code and the region's side.
sections.why: Automatic codes keep the labels consistent.
sections.watch_out: Codes count per region, so inserting a point earlier renumbers the points after it.

sections.name: link
sections.title: Link only when both ends exist
sections.what: Creates a link between two points only when both exist and are different; otherwise nothing is added.
sections.why: Stops links pointing at missing points.
sections.watch_out: A broken link is dropped silently, so it will not raise an error.

sections.name: industries
sections.title: Industry links from career data
sections.what: Creates one node for each industry found in the career entries and their key projects, and connects each industry to every career entry that worked in it. The text for each industry names the companies it came from.
sections.why: Likely reason: this lets the brain picture show which industries connect to which roles.
sections.watch_out: Company names are cut at the first comma, so two companies whose names begin the same way will show the same label.

sections.name: methods
sections.title: Methods, skills and build links
sections.what: Creates nodes for each method a career entry used (problem statements, frameworks and key project problems), for each technical skill, and for each build, except Career OS, which appears as a curiosity instead. It connects builds to their skills, their originating role and the matching methods, and chains the mental models in each family together in order.
sections.why: Likely reason: the source lists are separate, and this block turns them into one connected web so related items can be shown together.
sections.watch_out: Builds are matched to skills by tag text in lower case, so a tag spelled differently in the skills list and in the build will silently fail to connect.

sections.name: curiosityBuilds
sections.title: Curiosity and craft links
sections.what: Adds the right side of the brain: curiosities, research threads, and craft themes such as storytelling, satellite control and cricket. It then connects each one to the builds and career entries it relates to.
sections.why: Likely reason: the mental models file describes the left side as logic and the right side as curiosity and craft, and this block follows that split.
sections.watch_out: Many links use hard-coded project slugs, such as abacus and watchtower, and a renamed slug quietly stops linking without any error.

summary: Builds the hero brain map: a left and a right side of labelled points for roles, industries, methods, builds, curiosities and mental models, joined by real links from the data. Only part of the file was available to review.
purpose: Supplies the points and links that the home page brain draws, with codes such as R100.
why: The header comment says the left side is work and logic and the right side is curiosity and craft, and that links come from real relationships in the data.
how: 1) Defines the fixed list of regions. 2) Provides an add function that gives each point a code within its region. 3) Provides a link function that joins only points that exist. 4) Adds role points from the battle data, each with a photo and a link to the experience section. 5) Later sections, not visible here, add the industry, method and curiosity points.
inputs: Battle, build, project, curiosity, research thread, skill, mental model and photo data.
outputs: The region list, the point list and the link list.
risks: Letters for model families come from fixed lists, so a sixth left family would get no letter. Links to missing points are dropped silently.
debug: If a point is missing, check its id and region name. Codes count per region, so they shift when points are added earlier. If the brain is empty on the home page, check the exports, because the route file imports brainNodes and brainLinks and they are not visible here.
